text:
The Canadiens have a great record and an uneasy fan base, and both are earned. Montreal is 12-4-4 with 28 points, but the Ivan Demidov story has dominated the week, with speculation about surgery and a lot of noise around his name, alongside reports that Nick Suzuki has been playing through an injury. Saturday's 4-1 loss to a Colorado team missing Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar didn't calm anyone.

The standings are ahead of the play. Montreal has taken 48% of all expected goals (the quality of chances) and allows 3.52 expected goals per 60 minutes. Our points model has them about 7.5 points above what their play has earned, and the goaltending is most of it: the team has allowed 10.5 fewer goals than its chances, and Jacob Fowler has saved 3.6 above expected over his last five starts.

The good news is in the lineup's young core. Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson have taken 58% of the chances as a pair. Cole Caufield made franchise history this month and is on pace for a career year, and his line with Suzuki and Juraj Slafkovsky has outscored teams 6-2, even with Slafkovsky running a little cold. Arber Xhekaj has become a real defenseman, carrying the puck out with confidence, and a target for referees, depending on who you read.

Our playoff odds sit at 65%. What we'd watch: Demidov's health, and whether the save percentage holds while the chances against stay high.
